_comment: Adopted property tax rates per $100 of taxable value, by taxing unit.
A property's rate is the sum of every unit that taxes it: the county, its city (if
incorporated), its school district, and any county-wide special districts.
This exists because a statewide average is a poor stand-in where rates vary by school
district. In Lubbock County the spread is real: a Lubbock ISD property inside the city
totals 1.769%, the same house in Frenship ISD totals 2.059% — a 16% difference in the
single largest operating expense a landlord carries.
Public improvement districts are deliberately excluded: they apply only to parcels inside
specific developments, and membership cannot be determined from the parcel record. Where
one applies it is additive, so a PID property will be taxed slightly more than shown.

48303.source: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts, 2025 Statewide Report of Tax Rates

TX.headline: The seller's tax bill is not the tax bill you will get.
TX.detail: Texas caps the taxable value of a homesteaded property at 10% growth a year, and grants exemptions that reduce it further. The appraised market value shown here is not capped — the taxable value the current owner is billed on sits below it, often far below on a long-held property. A buyer inherits none of that: the exemptions come off, the cap resets, and the first bill is assessed on full market value. Do not underwrite from the seller's tax bill or from a tax estimate built on their taxable value. This app assesses tax on your purchase price, which is the right basis for a new owner.
